text:
Predicates:
TwinOrTriplet(x) ::: x is a twin or triplet.
SpendTimeWithSiblings(x) ::: x spends a lot of time hanging out with and playing with siblings.
SameAgeSiblings(x, y) ::: x and y are siblings of the same age.
ComplainsAboutSiblings(x) ::: x complains often about annoying siblings.
LiveAtHomeRegularly(x) ::: x lives at home regularly.
DevelopsStrongBonds(x) ::: x develops strong bonds with family members.
Premises:
∀x (TwinOrTriplet(x) → SpendTimeWithSiblings(x)) ::: If people are twins or triplets, then they spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with siblings.
∀x ∀y (SameAgeSiblings(x, y) → TwinOrTriplet(x) ∨ TwinOrTriplet(y)) ::: If people have siblings who are the same age, then they are twins or triplets.
∀x (ComplainsAboutSiblings(x) → SameAgeSiblings(x, y)) ::: If people complain often about annoying siblings, then they have siblings who are the same age.
∀x (¬LiveAtHomeRegularly(x) → ¬DevelopsStrongBonds(x)) ::: If people do not live at home regularly, then they do not develop strong bonds with family members.
∀x (SpendTimeWithSiblings(x) → ¬LiveAtHomeRegularly(x)) ::: If people spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with siblings, then they often did not live at home regularly.
Conclusion:
(TwinOrTriplet(Luke) ∧ DevelopsStrongBonds(Luke)) ∨ (¬TwinOrTriplet(Luke) ∧ ¬DevelopsStrongBonds(Luke)) ::: Luke is either both a twin or triplet and develops strong bonds, or neither.  
Question statement:
∃x (SpendTimeWithSiblings(x)) ::: Luke spends a lot of time hanging out and playing with his siblings (uncertain, as the premises do not specify Luke's behavior explicitly).
